'''Hyperspace''' travel in the campaign era: hyperlanes, jump beacons, hyperdrive classes and how long a journey takes.

The exploration of hyperspace happened concurrently with the expansion of the HoloNet, and went through three distinct technology phases.  For much of galactic history, starships lacked the computing power to calculate safe routes and were confined to jumps within networks of jump beacons. In war, this allowed navies to effectively pin ships at a certain point by disabling a beacon.

=== Summary of Hyperspace Technologies&#32; ===

* '''S-threads''' - the underlying infrastructure
*** HoloNet transceivers were placed within S-thread beacons, and when a ship (or homing beacon signal) crossed an S-thread, the event was logged. [[Homing beacon/Legends|Fandom]]
*** S-thread boosters - could create new hyperspace routes and keep existing ones open. They could be deployed in realspace or in hyperspace, and were expensive to use
* '''Jump/hyperspace beacons '''- the navigation network were massive super computers, containing local hypersapce data which visiting ships could download and establish their flight plan. 
*** Explicitly '''stationary''', moored in open space between systems and ships hopped from beacon to beacon.
* '''Hyperlanes''' - A properly charted hyperlane was a cleared, continuously safe corridor. On the big hyperlanes there were no mandatory stops, no beacon hops, no realspace reversions. A ship could enter at one end and exit at the other. 
*** On smaller lanes, occasional hops and re-aligning to another beacon was needed. Hyperlanes also were more direct in their path as better routes were discovered - beacons meandered. 
*** Hyperdrives also became faster during these later centuries.

'''Hyperdrive speed  (\~4,000 BBY to 19 BBY)'''

* Hyperdrive speed was rated on an inverse class scale — the faster the drive, the lower the rating. The class acted as a multiplier on a given base travel time. A Class 2 hyperdrive took twice the base time; the Millennium Falcon's Class 0.5 took only half. [[Hyperdrive/Legends|Fandom]]
* Most military starships were using Class 1, 2 or 3 hyperdrives. Industrial freighters and haulers used Class 3 or Class 4. Civilian ships used Class 5 or above.
* On a well-charted major hyperlane, travel took roughly 8 hours per galactic grid square at Class 1. A Class 1 drive travelling the Rimma Trade Route from Sullust to Thyferra — 4 grid squares — would take approximately 24 hours. [https://swse.fandom.com/wiki/Hyperspace_Travel_Times Fandom]
* A single galactic grid square on the standard map is approximately 1,500 parsecs, so Class 1 effectively covered \~1,500 parsecs in 8 hours

=== FACTORS THAT AFFECTED SPEED IN ALL ERAS ===

* Route quality mattered enormously — whether a cleared hyperlane existed for a continuous journey, and how much stellar matter (planets, stars, asteroids, nebulae) was in the path, since ships could not travel in a straight line through obstacles.
* Travel in the Deep Core was slower due to the dense concentration of stars, whereas the Outer Rim allowed faster transit because there was less to navigate around.
* A power drop in the hyperdrive — caused by a malfunction or hyperdrive damage would increase travel time.
* Pirates and Hutts tampering with beacon data in the ancient era could redirect ships entirely, adding enormous unintended journey time or resulting in ambush

'''S-threads - the underlying infrastructure'''

* S-threads are hyperspatial structures — essentially fixed lanes or threads running through hyperspace itself. Infrastructure, not navigation aids per se — they were the substrate the HoloNet and tracking systems used, not something a pilot aimed for to navigate.
* Think of them like invisible fence-lines strung across hyperspace — ships don't aim for them, they simply cross them as they travel, and those crossings are recorded.
* Ships traveling through hyperspace crossed at least one S-thread per hour. [[Homing beacon/Legends|Fandom]]

=== Hyperspace Lane Discovery Timeline ===

Five major super-hyperroutes of the galaxy (per the Essential Atlas) are:Perlemian Trade Route (H1), Corellian Run (H2), Corellian Trade Spine (H3), Rimma Trade Route (H4), and Hydian Way (H5).

Early hyperlane travel (25000 BBY era) used the S-thread beacon method, requiring multiple stops. Later lanes (4000 BBY onwards) were continuous routes requiring no reversion to realspace.

c. 27,000 BBY — Koros Trunk Line

c. 25,000–24,000 BBY — Corellian Run

c. 25,000 BBY — Corellian Trade Spine (initial spur)

c. 5,500 BBY — Rimma Trade Route

c. 5,000 BBY — Goluud Corridor

c. 5,000 BBY — Daragon Trail

c. 4,000 BBY — Ootmian Pabol (obsoleted)

c. 3,705–3,694 BBY — Hydian Way

c. 3,701–3,699 BBY — Seswenna Expansion

=== S-thread boosters ===

* S-thread boosters were technology that could create new hyperspace routes and keep existing ones open. They could be deployed in realspace or in hyperspace, with the latter called non-mass S-thread boosters. [[S-thread booster/Legends|Fandom]]
* Over the millennia following the settlement of the Koros system around 27,500 BBY and culminating shortly before the founding of the Galactic Republic in 25,053 BBY, hyperspace scouts used S-thread boosters to chart and maintain the Koros Trunk Line connecting the Koros system to Coruscant. So S-thread boosters predate the Republic itself. [[S-thread booster/Legends|Fandom]]
* S-thread boosters were extremely expensive to use. [[S-thread booster/Legends|Fandom]]

'''Jump/hyperspace beacons — the navigation network'''

These are the things pilots actually navigated ''to'':

* Beacons were massive supercomputers moored in open space '''between''' systems, specifically to avoid the gravitational effects of stars and planets. Each recorded local hyperspace data, which visiting ships could download. A beacon interfaced with a ship's flight plan and transmitted relevant astrogational information within its network. A local network could require as many as twenty beacons. [[Hyperspace beacon/Legends|Fandom]]
* They were known to be in use in the Tion Cluster as early as 25,100 BBY 
* Reliability of available data was only about 80%. [[Hyperspace beacon/Legends|Fandom]]
* The Salin Corridor, one of the oldest hyperlanes in the Outer Rim, was forged by Xim the Despot's empire and maintained by a "lighthouse network" of jump beacons. [[The galaxy/Legends|Fandom]]
* Beacon route travel was slow and laborious - not a single sustained hyperspace transit. In the early days of the Galactic Republic, hyperspace travel via beacons required numerous reversions to realspace to ensure safe passage. Each hop meant dropping out of hyperspace, re-acquiring the next beacon, downloading updated astrogation data, and jumping again.

=== Who maintained them ===

* The Bureau of Ships and Services (BoSS) — a separate body — was not attached to any one government and remained omnipresent across Republic, Empire, and New Republic eras. On at least two occasions it used beacon access as leverage to end wars, including threatening to withhold navigational data to force an end to the First Alsakan Conflict. That's remarkable institutional power — essentially holding the galaxy's road network hostage. [[Bureau of Ships and Services/Legends|Fandom]]
* The beacons were later maintained and patrolled by the Republic Spacelane Bureau. [[Hyperspace beacon/Legends|Fandom]]
* The Republic Spacelane Bureau also fought to end private control of hyperlane data and established a protected set of beacons for major pathways, liberating them from privately held charts. [[Hyperdrive/Legends|Fandom]]

=== Vulnerability and Hyperspace warfare ===

* Pirates and Hutts sometimes reprogrammed beacons to transmit incorrect coordinates, sending ships into deep space for ambush. [[Hyperspace beacon/Legends|Fandom]]
* By 4100 BBY, navigation computers had advanced to the point that jump beacons were no longer needed, making the military control of hyperspace routes far more difficult — blockading one route simply pushed ships onto alternative ones. [[Space warfare/Legends|Fandom]]
* However, statistically speaking, only a few of these routes could be traversed quickly, and a military force that controlled the fast routes could rapidly redeploy to intercept an adversary using the slow ones. 
* Hyperlanes thus determined the strategic geography of space warfare, and fleets repeatedly battled over the same planets on significant hyperspace routes,

=== Hyperspace Lanes in detail ===

=== PRE-REPUBLIC ERA ===

'''c. 27,000 BBY — Koros Trunk Line'''

One of the oldest known hyperlanes, connecting Coruscant to Koros Major (later Empress Teta) in the Deep Core. Predates even the Rakatan Infinite Empire. Discovered using the primitive S-thread beacon method, requiring frequent reversions to realspace.

=== EARLY REPUBLIC ERA ===

'''c. 25,000 BBY — Perlemian Trade Route'''

Originally called ''The Axis''. One of the five great super-hyperroutes. Blazed shortly after the founding of the Galactic Republic, linking Coruscant to Ossus and the Tion Cluster in the northeastern Outer Rim. Along with the Corellian Run, it forms the borders of ''The Slice''— the most densely settled corridor of the galaxy. Instrumental in rapid Republic colonisation of the eastern galaxy.

'''c. 25,000–24,000 BBY — Corellian Run'''

Mapped during roughly the same period as the Perlemian. Began at Coruscant, looped around the Deep Core through Corellia, and extended outward to Ryloth and beyond. Made Corellia an economic superpower in the early Republic. With the Perlemian, it defined The Slice.

'''c. 25,000 BBY — Corellian Trade Spine (initial spur)'''

First established as a spur of the Corellian Run around the same time as the great early lanes, though it was not completed in full until approximately 5,500 BBY. Built incrementally over millennia, eventually stretching from Corellia toward the galactic edge, past the Greater Javin region.

=== OLD REPUBLIC ERA ===

'''c. 5,500 BBY — Rimma Trade Route'''

Established by Tapani Sector merchants. Ran from Abregado-rae in the Core Worlds out to the Kathol Sector in the Outer Rim, passing through Fondor, Sullust, and Sluis Van. Also around this time the Corellian Trade Spine was completed to its full extent. The Rimma became a critical link between the Core and the southwestern Outer Rim.

'''c. 5,000 BBY — Goluud Corridor'''

Discovered by hyperspace explorers Gav and Jori Daragon. A route through the Starswarm Cluster, approved by the Hyperspace Navigator’s Guild but marked as risky. It served as the precursor to the Daragon Trail.

'''c. 5,000 BBY — Daragon Trail'''

An extension of the Goluud Corridor, blazed by Gav and Jori Daragon in a single, uncharted blind jump from Koros Major all the way to Korriban in Sith space — the longest successful blind jump in recorded history. Its discovery inadvertently made contact with the Sith Empire, triggering the Great Hyperspace War. Part of it later became the Carbonite Run.

'''c. 4,000 BBY — Ootmian Pabol (obsoleted)'''

An older secondary route running from the Core out through Hutt Space. It became obsolete in approximately 4,000 BBY when a supernova in the Kyyr system destroyed the route, diverting traffic to the Corellian Run and accelerating the decline of Nal Hutta as a trade hub.

=== NOT YET DISCOVERED ===

'''c. 3,705–3,694 BBY — Hydian Way'''

Blazed by Freia Kallea of Brentaal IV and later completed with the help of Duros scout Banu Hydia, for whom it was named. The only super-hyperroute to cross the entire galactic disc, from the Corporate Sector to the southern Outer Rim. Scouting began in 3,705 BBY; Kallea’s ship was crippled by Neimoidian saboteurs, stranding her on Nuvar for six years. The final segment, the Hydian Spur, was charted in 3,694 BBY. The Hydian Way fundamentally altered galactic civilisation by opening up regions beyond The Slice for the first time.

* The Hydian Way completion (3,694 BBY) is generally considered the moment the galaxy became fully connected as a single economic civilisation.

'''c. 3,701–3,699 BBY — Seswenna Expansion'''

Charted by Neimoidian scouts during the period when Freia Kallea was stranded and unable to complete the Hydian Way. The Neimoidians scouted this southward extension from Malastare, reaching the Rimma Trade Route south of Eriadu, capitalising on Kallea’s absence.

=== NOTES ===

* Hundreds of secondary and thousands of minor routes were blazed throughout galactic history; dates for most are unrecorded.
